question: According to Article 51 A (a) of the Constitution of India, it shall be the duty of every Indian citizen to abide by the constitutions and respect its ideals and institutions.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1.**__** **

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Article 51A (a) of the Constitution of India states** that it is the** fundamental duty of every citizen of India to abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the national flag, and the national anthem.**
 
• This duty is considered an important aspect of **citizenship in India and reflects the commitment of citizens towards the values and principles enshrined in the Constitution.**
 
• It is the responsibility of every citizen to uphold the **democratic principles, protect the sovereignty of the country, and promote national unity and integrity.​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **Secularism in a constitution** refers to the principle that the state and its institutions are separate from religion, and that the state does not favor or promote any particular religion or religious beliefs.

 
 
• This means that the state is neutral in matters of religion, and individuals are free to practice their own religion without interference or discrimination from the state.
 
 
• Many countries around the world have included secularism in their constitutions.
 
• For example, the I**ndian Constitution, which was adopted in 1950, enshrines secularism as a fundamental principle. Article 25 of the Indian Constitution guarantees the freedom of conscience and the right to freely profess, practice, and propagate religion subject to public order, morality and health.**
 
 
 
 
 
• **​Socialism is an economic and political ideology** that emphasizes collective or state ownership and control of the means of **production, distribution, and exchange, as well as the goal of achieving greater economic equality and social justice.**
 
• **Democracy** is a system of government where the power is held by the people, either directly or through elected representatives. It is derived from the Greek words **"demos," meaning "people," and "kratos," meaning "rule."**
 
 
• In a **democratic society, citizens **have the right to participate in the **political process, such as voting in elections, expressing their opinions, and holding their elected officials accountable.**
 
• Democracy values the principles of** freedom, equality, and justice**. It promotes individual rights and freedoms, and allows for the peaceful resolution of conflicts through open and fair dialogue.
 
• While democracy is often associated with** Western countries**, there are various forms of democratic systems in different regions of the world, such as parliamentary, presidential, and constitutional democracies.
